stories.headline: Fantasy football buzz: Saints place RB Travis Etienne Jr. on IR
stories.summary: Eric Moody evaluates which Saints RBs could see a greater share of the backfield after Etienne's move to IR.
stories.body:
Everything that happens in the NFL has additional context when viewed from a fantasy football perspective. From position battles to injuries and so much more, the news cycle will constantly affect player values in fantasy football.

Our fantasy football buzz file, with contributions from our ESPN fantasy writers and our NFL Nation reporters, aims to provide fantasy managers with the intel they need as news breaks around the league.

Oct. 1: Saints place RB Etienne Jr. on IR

By Eric Moody

The New Orleans Saints placed RB Travis Etienne Jr. on injured reserve with a hamstring injury, meaning he'll miss at least four games. With New Orleans' Week 8 bye, the earliest he can return is Week 9. That leaves Alvin Kamara and Kendre Miller in line for more work in the backfield.

Kamara should get the first chance at leading the backfield. Etienne had taken on the largest share of the workload in Week 3 and finished with 13 carries despite leaving in the third quarter, while Kamara had nine and Miller had four.

Kamara hasn't been very efficient this season (2.8 YPC), but more touches could put him back in the RB2 conversation. He should see plenty of carries and remain involved in the passing game, giving him a solid floor as a flex option.

Miller should be rostered in 12-team leagues. Double-digit touches are possible with Etienne out, but I'd keep him on the bench until we get a better idea of how New Orleans plans to split the work.

Don't forget about CJ Donaldson, either. Coach Kellen Moore gave him the Saints' first touch inside the 10-yard line last week. If that continues, Donaldson could have a role near the goal line, even if Kamara and Miller handle most of the work.

Kamara is the one I'd feel comfortable starting right away. Miller belongs on rosters in 12-team leagues, while Donaldson is more of a deeper league player to monitor.

Dolphins move towards split backfield to replace Achane

By Marcel Louis-Jacques

Miami Dolphins running back Ollie Gordon II was one of the most popular adds in fantasy this week. The former Doak Walker Award winner offers rare size for the position and handled a 20-touch workload in place of De'Von Achane in Week 3.

We all know opportunity is a premium commodity in fantasy, but it's important to remember that Gordon was the Dolphins' only other active running back last week. Jaylen Wright, the former fourth-round pick, has seldom seen the field during his three-year career but ran for 107 yards and a touchdown on 24 carries filling in for Achane against the Jets last season.

Wright offers sub-4.40 speed and a versatile skill set. Speaking to Wright and Gordon this week, they sound ready to share the workload moving forward.

Dolphins Coach Jeff Hafley envisions a split backfield, so expect them to ride with the hot hand.

Sept. 30: TNF injury updates, 10 trends to know for Week 4

By Michael F. Florio

Rico Dowdle did not practice to start the week and is out for the Pittsburgh Steelers' "Thursday Night Football" matchup with the Cleveland Browns. With Dowdle sidelined last week, Jaylen Warren handled the bulk of the opportunities, playing 90% of the snaps and garnering 17 carries and four targets. Warren finished with 176 total yards and 20.6 fantasy points (RB8).

Warren has a chance to build off of that in Cleveland, as the Browns have allowed the sixth-most yards on outside runs and have missed tackles at the sixth-highest rate in the NFL. Warren should be started over David Montgomery, Quinshon Judkins, Omarion Hampton, Rhamondre Stevenson and Jadarian Price.

Trends to know for Week 4

Defenses have altered the way they play Drake Maye since last season's playoffs. Teams are rushing four men -- or fewer, at times -- at a high rate against the New England Patriots but have still been able to create quick pressure. Last week, the Jacksonville Jaguars rushed four or fewer on 82% of dropbacks and still created pressure in under 2.5 seconds, on average. Each team has played Cover 6 at least 15% of the time against Maye.

Simply put, teams are able to get to Maye quickly without blitzing, meaning they are able to drop more players into coverage. Maye has to make quick decisions, and it is not allowing enough time for his receivers to consistently get open. It also has seemingly sped the clock up in his head.

I think Maye will eventually figure it out, and his value will likely never be lower, especially in dynasty leagues. These struggles create a trade-for opportunity. However, until we see Maye figure it out, it is very tough to trust him in redraft leagues.

Bryce Young faces a Detroit Lions defense that has allowed the most passing yards and the second-most touchdowns to QBs. Every QB to face Detroit has scored at least 23 fantasy points, and they've respectively finished QB8, QB1 and QB3.
Bhayshul Tuten has forced 15 missed tackles on outside runs (second most), and the Cincinnati Bengals have the sixth-highest rate of missed tackles on such runs (40%).
Bucky Irving, who has the fourth-most rushing yards on outside runs, faces the Green Bay Packers, who have allowed the most yards on those runs.
Rashee Rice had eight of his nine targets come against zone defense last week. The Las Vegas Raiders play zone 81% of the time.
Garrett Wilson has a 62% target share against man coverage, by far the highest in the NFL. He faces the Chicago Bears, who have played man at the fourth-highest rate.
DJ Moore has a 35% target share against man coverage, and the Patriots play man at the second-highest rate in the NFL.
Stefon Diggs has a team-high 30% target share against man coverage, which the Indianapolis Colts play at the third-highest rate in the league. The Colts also have allowed the most yards to slot receivers, and Diggs has lined up in the slot for 51% of his routes so far this season.
The Lions have allowed the most yards and touchdowns to tight ends. Darren Waller is coming off season highs in snap rate ( 51%) and targets (eight).
Cam Ward has 717 career dropbacks. Of QBs with that many in the Next Gen Stats era, he ranks last in yards per attempt (5.8) and success rate (36.5%). Only Zach Wilson (-0.25) has a lower EPA per dropback (-0.23).

Add Braelon Allen, stash Zach Charbonnet if you need RBs

By Tristan H. Cockcroft

How you doin', Vampire league managers?

Better yet, how about you zero-RB strategizers?

The 2026 season hasn't been the friendliest to those who went the cheap route at running back, at least not so far. Through three weeks, only two running backs selected outside the top 30 at the position on average have scored as many as 15 fantasy points in a game: Chuba Hubbard (twice) and Kyle Monangai. And anyone playing the Vampire format or going full zero-RB might not have even drafted either player, considering Hubbard went 34th and Monangai 37th; that'd be right around the four-running back average per team in the format.

A running back has scored at least 15 fantasy points on 35 occasions. Twenty-six, or 74%, came from top-15 positional picks. Fourteen, or 40%, came from the top eight. And six of the 11 games worth 25-plus points came from top-three backs Jahmyr Gibbs, Bijan Robinson and Jonathan Taylor.

That's not to dissuade zero-RB drafters, who have had success employing the strategy in the past and will probably fare better in the coming weeks as injuries and role changes take hold at the position. Besides, you've got the team you've got at this point, so you need to make the best of it.

Running back has been a particular focus of a couple of my teams this and last week, including in the Vampire league specifically, where the position's ho-hum stats have dug me a 0-3 hole. A pair of backfields that are not the altogether-too-obvious Miami Dolphins -- new leading man Ollie Gordon II was predictably the No. 1 free agent pickup overnight -- have my attention:

New York Jets: It's Braelon Allen, not Gordon, who was my primary focus on the pickups front, after news that usual starter Breece Hall's thigh injury late in Week 3 is a week-to-week, rather than day-to-day, injury. A big, powerful back, Allen might share rushing work with Isaiah Davis while Hall heals, but Allen is a capable fill-in starter with a good matchup in Week 4 (@CHI). I'm anticipating 12-15 carries and top odds on any goal-line carries, and that'd be a pretty good find off free agency for those seeking running back help (which should really be everyone).

Seattle Seahawks: Jadarian Price's fumbling problem is clearly an issue, as it's rare to see a first-round draft pick and Week 1 starter benched three games into his NFL career. Price's lost fumbles in back-to-back games -- 13 carries apart -- got him sidelined for much of Week 3, though Emanuel Wilson didn't do much in Price's stead (1.4 FPTS, 1.6 YPC) after having decent garbage-time stats in Week 2. But then there's Zach Charbonnet, who has one more game to miss while on the PUP list but is eligible to have his practice window opened, something that could happen in the coming days. All indications are that Charbonnet will be ready to play during the season's first half, and if he's back by mid-October, he'd at least be returning at the right time to swiftly reclaim the lion's share of the rushing work. And with all the injuries thus far, fantasy managers might not have been able to keep an IL slot available while waiting for him. If you've got one freed up and he's available in your league, Charbonnet is a worthy stash.

Sept. 29: Case Keenum to the Monday night rescue

By Michael F. Florio

Case Keenum was the star of the show on "Monday Night Football," emerging from third on the Bears' QB depth chart in Week 2 to make the Week 3 start, his first since Dec. 24, 2023. He threw for 247 yards and two touchdowns, completing 71% of his passes. He also added six rushing yards and a touchdown. He finished with 24.48 fantasy points, meaning he has more in one game than Drake Maye does on the season (21.6).

Keenum could be in line to start again in Week 4, and would be in play in superflex leagues against a Jets secondary that has been tough to pass on this season. Tyson Bagent would be the other Bears option while Caleb Williams recovers from his hamstring injury.

Kalif Raymond led the Bears in receiving yards for the second time in three weeks. He and Luther Burden III have been the Bears' top two target-getters in each game. Through three weeks, he is second on the team in targets. He should be the top WR waiver wire pickup, as he is available in almost 90% of leagues. Burden had a big night of his own, seeing a team-high 11 targets, turning them into seven catches for 61 yards and a touchdown. He also added in a 7-yard run. He leads the Bears in targets and has a 32% red zone target share. Burden is blossoming into the must-start option fantasy managers envisioned during draft season.

Both Colston Loveland and Rome Odunze just missed touchdowns. Loveland dove and was down just short of the goal line at the 1. Meanwhile, Odunze had an open touchdown slip through his hands. In total, Odunze turned six targets into three catches for 44 yards. Loveland finished with four catches for 31 yards on four targets. Both players' fantasy stocks remain down. Loveland is in play just because the lack of high-ceiling options at tight end. Odunze though is purely a flex option that should hit a good amount of benches until we see otherwise.
The Bears did not duplicate the rushing success that they had in 2025, but D'Andre Swift did have himself a nice showing. He played 70% of the snaps with 20 carries for 84 yards. He also caught two of three targets for four yards. While he did not score a touchdown, he was used often in the red zone. Kyle Monangai finished with 10 carries for 31 yards. He is a top insurance back but has had trouble finding standalone value.
It was a tough night for Jalen Hurts and the Eagles offense. The team's best drive was right before the half, where Hurts snapped the ball with one second left on the ticking clock and scored his first rushing touchdown of the season. He finished with 153 yards passing and an interception. He missed four plays while in the medical tent and Andy Dalton threw a goal line interception.
Saquon Barkley played 75% of the snaps and turned 15 carries into 82 yards. He saw two targets, catching one for -2 yards. Barkley has yet to score double-digit fantasy points in a game this season. The Eagles face two tough run defenses in their next two games (Rams, Jaguars) but it opens up after that. The next two weeks are an opportunity to acquire Barkley at a discount.
DeVonta Smith saw eight targets, catching six for 65 yards. Through three weeks, he has a 33% target share and a 48% air yard share. That usage could lead to a fantasy WR1 season. He is the only Eagles pass catcher that can be trusted weekly.
Dontayvion Wicks saw five targets, catching two for 32 yards. He has been the top red zone target for Hurts to start the season. That has him in play as a deep-league flex option. Rookie Makai Lemon is still operating as the WR3, but is starting to be used more. He caught three of four targets for 29 yards. He remains a bench stash.

Sept. 28: Jets, Saints grapple with RB injuries

By Michael F. Florio

New York Jets RB Breece Hall is week-to-week after suffering a quad injury on Sunday, per Ian Rapoport and Adam Schefter. Rapoport reported that the injury is not as significant as feared.

That leaves Braelon Allen and Isaiah Davis active for the Jets. I would anticipate that Allen, who has been the RB2 behind Hall for the past three years, starts and handles the majority of ground work. Both backs have handled limited volume in their careers, but Allen has been the superior runner of the two. He has a 51% success rate.

Davis is a bit of an explosive runner and has been effective as a pass catcher out of the backfield. While he does not have a touch this season, he has caught 75% of targets in his career and averaged 8.7 yards per reception.

Both Jets backs are worth adding in fantasy as this plays itself out in the coming weeks. Allen will be a flex option in a favorable matchup against the Chicago Bears.

Etienne to miss time with hamstring injury
New Orleans Saints coach Kellen Moore announced Monday that RB Travis Etienne Jr. has a hamstring injury that will force him to miss time. Moore did not reveal a specific timetable.

That leaves the Saints' backfield with Alvin Kamara and Kendre Miller. I would expect Kamara to handle the bulk of the passing downs, while the two will likely split the ground work.

Kamara has seen nine carries in each game he has played this season and racked up seven targets. The efficiency is gone, as he has averaged just 2.6 yards per touch. Still, volume keeps him in play as a potential flex option moving forward.

Miller is an option for those deep league players. He is the more efficient runner of the two, but we know the Saints are not going to just hand him the job over Kamara. Miller should see enough carries to be in the flex range in deep leagues. How the goal line work is distributed between the two will be huge for fantasy purposes.

Both are volume dependent flex options, with low floors, in a tough matchup against the Falcons next week.

Sept. 28: QB-depleted Giants trade for J.J. McCarthy, Bucs lose Baker Mayfield

By Eric Karabell

Quarterback J.J. McCarthy, the No. 10 pick in the 2024 NFL draft, is now a member of the New York Giants after they sent a fifth-round pick to the Minnesota Vikings for his services. In some ways, this is stunning. The Vikings gave up on McCarthy after one terrible season in which he completed only 57.6% of his throws and accrued more interceptions than touchdown passes. He is 23, but the Vikings might or might not be set with their future quarterback depending on how newcomer Kyler Murray performs. Early returns -- for Murray's performance and durability -- are quite mixed.

The Giants are taking a chance on an intriguing prospect even though McCarthy did not play well during his first active season. Then again, the Giants already have an intriguing quarterback prospect in Jaxson Dart, the No. 25 pick in the 2025 draft. Dart remains their future quarterback, but concussions marred his rookie campaign, and this season ended in Week 2 with major tears in his left knee. Nobody knows whether Dart can stay healthy for a full season, which is why this trade makes sense for the Giants.

For fantasy purposes, those who roster Dart in a keeper/dynasty league should already have been quite worried about his future in terms of staying on the field. This trade doesn't necessarily alter that. McCarthy missed his entire rookie season with a knee injury, too. The Giants add another body who, when healthy, needs to prove himself on the field. Dart has done that part already.

As for this season's Giants, veteran backup Jameis Winston seems likely to remain the starting quarterback for as long as he is healthy and competent. He was competent enough Sunday, leading the team to a 12-7 win over the Titans, even though he did little to aid fantasy managers statistically. Winston threw for only 118 yards, albeit in difficult weather conditions, but he avoided turnovers. The Winston who passed for 5,109 yards, 33 touchdowns and 30 interceptions for the 2019 Buccaneers is long gone.

Expect Winston to remain the starter, and assuming the Giants prefer Winston to act cautiously as a passer, merely directing the offense and attempting safe throws, it already impedes the upside for WRs Malik Nabers and Malachi Fields, and TE Isaiah Likely. RB Cam Skattebo earned 23 touches Sunday. His volume should remain high. If McCarthy were to replace Winston, it would not appear to aid Nabers, Fields and others, but that is because we don't know enough about McCarthy. One season proved little.

Still, McCarthy has some value for the rest of the 2026 season, as he becomes next in line to start, and for keeper/dynasty formats. McCarthy is young. Quarterbacks struggle to stay healthy in the NFL. It would not be surprising if McCarthy starts some games this season and plays competently, and who knows, perhaps he'll start next season if Dart is compromised. It is tough to assume McCarthy will perform well. His fantasy value rises a bit after this trade because the Vikings had made it abundantly clear they didn't want him around anymore, but the Giants have a franchise quarterback when healthy. The Vikings did not.

How Mayfield's absence affects the Bucs' offense
Tampa Bay Buccaneers QB Baker Mayfield left Sunday's game with a dislocated right thumb injury, and word came Monday that he will miss at least the next three weeks. Mayfield, off to a disappointing start statistically and rostered in 49.4% of ESPN standard leagues, is averaging only 11.7 points per game, a bit behind Cam Ward, Aaron Rodgers and Malik Willis. Mayfield will miss enticing games during the next two weeks versus the Green Bay Packers and Dallas Cowboys, and then the Buccaneers face the Pittsburgh Steelers and Carolina Panthers.

Jalon Daniels, an undrafted rookie from Kansas, assumes the starting role. Fantasy managers should be cautious in their pursuit, including in multi-QB and superflex formats, and we must downgrade wide receivers Emeka Egbuka, Chris Godwin Jr. and others. Daniels, who spent six seasons with the Jayhawks, enjoyed three seasons with at least 2,000 passing yards and 400 rushing yards, and rushed for 17 touchdowns during those seasons. He is not known for his accuracy or decision-making.

Sept. 28: Who got the ball on Sunday?

By Eric Moody

The box score doesn't tell you everything. Here are the roles and usage trends from Sunday that stood out to me.

Los Angeles Chargers at Buffalo Bills

The Chargers used a much more balanced backfield rotation in Week 3. Omarion Hampton still led the group with 27 snaps and 15 carries, but Keaton Mitchell was right behind him with 23 snaps and turned eight carries into 52 yards. Hampton also led the backfield with 25 snaps on first and second down, compared with 17 for Mitchell and 10 for Kimani Vidal, so he still appears to have the clearest hold on the early-down role.

The bigger concern for Hampton is his shrinking passing-game usage. He ran only six routes and saw one target, while Mitchell ran 14 routes and caught three passes, including a touchdown. Vidal also ran 10 routes. Mitchell's combination of increased early-down work, passing-game involvement and efficiency makes this look more like a committee than it did to start the season. He's worth adding where available, while Hampton's fantasy ceiling could be lower if this rotation continues.

This was supposed to be a chance for Oronde Gadsden to step up with David Njoku and Charlie Kolar injured. He dominated the tight end routes, but still split snaps with Hayden Rucci and saw just two targets. Tre' Harris, Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston combined for 18 targets. It's hard to trust anyone in the Chargers offense right now.

Carolina Panthers at Cleveland Browns

KC Concepcion's role took a step forward in Week 3. He played significant snaps in both 11 and 12 personnel, pushing Jerry Jeudy out of the No. 2 receiver role. The production hasn't followed yet, as Concepcion caught just two of nine targets for nine yards, but quarterback accuracy played a part. Deshaun Watson was off target on five of those nine throws, and those are the only five off-target passes Concepcion has seen on 20 targets this season. The usage remains encouraging, making him someone to add in deeper formats.

New York Jets at Detroit Lions

Kenyon Sadiq took advantage of an expanded role with Mason Taylor out, leading the tight end room in snaps, running 25 routes and drawing eight targets. He was also the Jets' primary tight end in 11 personnel, logging 23 snaps there compared with 11 for Jeremy Ruckert and five for Jelani Woods. Sadiq turned that usage into seven catches for 105 yards and a touchdown, giving him 12 receptions for 143 yards and a receiving score through three games, plus a rushing touchdown. His role could change when Taylor returns, but this breakout should make it difficult for the Jets to scale him back too much.

Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams both saw their roles dip in Week 3 as Detroit leaned more heavily on 12 and 13 personnel. After using 13 personnel just eight times over the first two weeks, the Lions used it 10 times in Week 3, only the sixth time under Dan Campbell they've reached double-digit 13-personnel plays. St. Brown dropped to 28 routes and eight targets, while Williams ran 29 routes with four targets. That's a noticeable decline from their first two games, so if Detroit continues using heavier personnel at this rate, it could lower the weekly volume and fantasy ceiling for both receivers.

Houston Texans at Indianapolis Colts

Josh Downs saw a major boost with Alec Pierce on injured reserve, drawing a team-high 10 targets and turning them into 12.7 fantasy points. He ran the third-most routes and remained one of the focal points of the passing game alongside Tyler Warren and Keenan Allen. Downs' snap rate dipped in some heavier personnel packages, but the target volume is what matters most for fantasy managers. With Pierce sidelined, Downs looks like a solid flex option in Week 4 against a Commanders defense that has allowed the ninth-most fantasy points per game to wide receivers.

Dalton Schultz's fantasy production fell off in Week 3 as Houston used more multiple-tight-end sets. That cut into his snaps and routes, and he finished with just three targets and 6.0 fantasy points after seeing 14 targets and scoring 26.0 fantasy points in Week 2. Schultz could still have useful weeks when Houston is forced to throw more, but his role looks less secure now, especially with Nico Collins returning and taking back a big share of the targets.

Kansas City Chiefs at Miami Dolphins

Rashee Rice's season-high 15.8 fantasy points wasn't the result of more playing time or increased slot usage. He actually played his fewest snaps of the season and ran fewer routes from the slot than he did in Weeks 1 and 2, while Kansas City used less 11 personnel and more 12 personnel. The difference was target volume. Rice caught seven of nine targets for 88 yards and has now topped 80 receiving yards in back-to-back games. That's encouraging, but fantasy managers should expect some regression if that target concentration comes back down.

Tennessee Titans at New York Giants

Cam Skattebo led the Giants backfield in snaps, routes run, touches (23) and fantasy points (13.0). However, he averaged just 3.0 yards per carry, while Najee Harris averaged 5.8 yards on nine carries. Skattebo remains a volume-based RB2, but it would be nice to see him become more efficient as a runner, especially in Week 4 against a Cardinals defense that has allowed the seventh most rushing yards per game.

Isaiah Likely opened the season with a huge Week 1, and while the fantasy production has cooled, his role keeps improving. His route participation has climbed each week, and he currently ranks 12th among tight ends in routes run. Likely still drew five targets against the Titans despite Jameis Winston attempting just 22 passes. The usage remains strong, making Likely a tight end fantasy managers should continue to hold.

Cincinnati Bengals at Pittsburgh Steelers

Jaylen Warren took full advantage of Rico Dowdle's absence, handling a true every-down role for the first time in his career. He led the Steelers backfield in snaps, routes, touches (20) and fantasy points (20.6). Warren also showed plenty of explosiveness, creating multiple chunk plays. If Dowdle remains out in Week 4 against the Browns, Warren should again see a heavy workload.

Seattle Seahawks at Washington Commanders

The Seahawks backfield became even more difficult to trust in Week 3. Emanuel Wilson led the team in carries (9) and handled the biggest share of early-down work, while Jadarian Price played just 19 snaps and saw much of his action late. Price still led the team in rushing with just 15 yards, which was disappointing behind Seattle's offensive line, and he also lost a fumble. George Holani mixed in heavily as well, especially in the passing game, and led the backfield with 10.8 fantasy points. With Zach Charbonnet expected back soon, Price's role looks too unstable to trust in fantasy lineups.

New England Patriots at Jacksonville Jaguars

Brian Thomas Jr.'s role took another hit. Jakobi Meyers and Parker Washington have clearly moved ahead of him in Jacksonville's receiver rotation, while rookie Josh Cameron is also cutting into his playing time. Thomas is even losing work in heavier personnel packages, which makes the situation more concerning than just a quiet box score. For fantasy managers, Thomas is becoming difficult to trust as anything more than a risky flex until his role starts to grow again.

The Patriots settled into a true split backfield, but Rhamondre Stevenson still handled the more valuable work. Stevenson shared early-down snaps with TreVeyon Henderson while also taking most of the passing-down, short-yardage and goal-line opportunities. Henderson remains the more explosive option, but his limited receiving role makes him much more dependent on big plays. The bigger issue is an offense that hasn't been very productive, which limits the ceiling for both backs. Stevenson is the safer fantasy option right now, while Henderson is more of a boom-or-bust flex until his role grows.

Arizona Cardinals at San Francisco 49ers

George Kittle set a season high in snaps, led the 49ers with seven targets and finished with 26.2 fantasy points. With all of San Francisco's injuries at wide receiver, Kittle should remain a focal point of the passing game, especially with Brock Purdy playing at such a high level. Purdy has a 93.7 Total QBR this season, the highest by any quarterback through his team's first three games since the metric was introduced in 2006. Three of the other four QBs on the list went on to win MVP that season.

Jeremiyah Love took a clear step forward in Week 3, handling over 80% of Arizona's early-down snaps after a more limited role to start the season. He finished with a season high 26 touches and 21.9 fantasy points Tyler Allgeier still controls some of the passing-down and goal-line work, which caps Love's receiving and touchdown upside.

Minnesota Vikings at Tampa Bay Buccaneers

The Buccaneers' backfield is starting to look more defined. Bucky Irving and Kenny Gainwell had eerily similar snap and route totals, but Irving handled most of the early-down work while Gainwell took more of the passing-down snaps. Irving remains the best fantasy option and has reached at least 15 touches in every game, even though his efficiency dipped in Week 3 with 3.1 yards per carry. Gainwell's standalone fantasy value is limited, but he would become a much more relevant option if Irving were to miss time.

Baltimore Ravens at Dallas Cowboys

Javonte Williams dominated the Cowboys backfield, finishing with 21 touches and 18.3 fantasy points against the Ravens. He's had at least 15 touches in every game this season. Behind him, the backup role has been a revolving door. Tyler Goodson is now the primary backup after being active over Emari Demercado in Week 3, making him the Dallas insurance back to roster in deeper leagues.

Las Vegas Raiders at New Orleans Saints

Alvin Kamara assumed lead back duties after Travis Etienne Jr. aggravated his hamstring injury in the third quarter and did not return against the Raiders. Kamara played more snaps and had more touches over Kendre Miller following Etienne's departure.

Los Angeles Rams at Denver Broncos

Kyren Williams continues to separate himself from Blake Corum despite the Rams still rotating their backs by drive. Williams handled the larger workload in Week 3 and turned it into 21 touches and 21.9 fantasy points, including a career-high 70 receiving yards. Corum managed just 15 rushing yards and has yet to record a red-zone carry this season. Williams has now produced at least 15 fantasy points in every game and remains a high end RB2, while Corum is best viewed as one of the top insurance backs in the league.

stories.headline: How Man City players, staff are handling Premier League verdict
stories.summary: As the reaction to Man City's guilty verdict continues to ripple across the sporting world, the club's internal messaging is very much one of confidence and carrying on. It may be easier said than done.
stories.body:
The strength of the judgement against Manchester City, following their legal case with the Premier League, has shocked the club, its employees and their players. Most of those inside the City Football Academy (CFA) accept that the verdict -- made public for the first time on Tuesday -- is a worst-case scenario.

There's been speculation and discussion on and off at the CFA for more than three years since the charges were announced in February 2023 about what might happen. It was always viewed internally as highly unlikely that every count of financial misconduct would be proved.

City insist they are innocent -- a message that's come from the top, namely chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak and CEO Ferran Soriano -- and many employees want to give the club the benefit of the doubt. They enjoy working for City and feel that they've been well looked after over the years.

In that respect, many people ESPN spoke for this story with are choosing to believe the conviction of Khaldoon and Soriano. At the very least, the majority of these staff members are prepared to wait until after the appeal is heard before passing judgement.

- Legal explainer: Man City have been charged. Now what?

- Marcotti: Hard to see how Man City come back from seismic scandal

- Ogden: Does Man City's guilty verdict ruin Guardiola's legacy?

Many staff members are also fans and as such, they are personally invested as well as professionally. City are a big club and a major employer, but since the Abu Dhabi takeover in 2008, they club's owners have done a good job of creating a family feel and a sense of shared purpose. More than 700 employees attended a UK all-staff meeting in the first week of this three-week international break, while players are away on duty with their national teams.

There is, however, a cloud hanging over the CFA, and the mood in general has been described to ESPN as nervous. Soriano, in his video message to staff on Tuesday, insisted it should be business as usual, but in the absence of any real information about what sanctions might follow, there's genuine worry about what the future could hold.

The same goes for the players. With many of City's senior squad away on international duty, some have had direct contact with the club, while others have not. One agent of a first-team player told ESPN that his client is "calm" about the situation and is happy with the public reassurances offered by senior executives. There is, though, an acceptance that things could change depending on the result of the appeal -- which has yet to be filed, but must be lodged by the close of business on Friday, Oct. 2 -- and any punishment handed down.

Player concerns

Speculation over considerable sporting sanctions is causing the most concern, sources tell ESPN. After all, City's players chose to go to the Etihad Stadium to play in the Premier League and the Champions League while getting the opportunity to win trophies. They need to be playing well at the highest level to earn international call-ups and to play at major international tournaments.

For that reason, one representative of a City first-teamer has privately questioned the sense in punishing current players who were not at the club when the alleged transgressions occurred between 2009 and 2018. Another agent has told ESPN that the players -- many of whom arrived or penned new deals after February, 2023, when the charges were first announced -- knew what they were signing up for because possible punishments have been widely known for a while.

Sources have told ESPN that the Professional Football Association (PFA) have made themselves available to talk to players about issues arising from the verdict. They helped a number of players at the end of last season when Southampton were expelled from the play-offs because a staff member was caught spying on opponents' training sessions; in that case, a significant sporting sanction was handed down for an incident that didn't involve the team, but did directly impact them.

It's unclear how many City players have clauses in their contracts to protect themselves in the event of relegation, or a points deduction so severe that it prevents the club from challenging for the title or playing in Europe for a number of years. "There may be a few tough lessons for players whose agents focus purely on how much their client is paid," one agent told ESPN.

Sources have told ESPN that other clubs are monitoring City's situation carefully and work is already going on in the background to find out what protections -- if any -- players have in their contracts, and whether or not they are accessible for transfer talks. Questions are also being asked privately about whether there's an appetite -- even at this early stage -- to consider alternative options away from the Etihad in the future.

The football department are keen to minimise any distractions. Manager Enzo Maresca is expected to address the verdict when his players return to the CFA next week, and his message is likely to centre on a need to remain focused on football.

Whether that's possible or not is another matter. The story has already followed City's players wherever they've played during the international break. Norway manager Stale Solbakken was asked about Erling Haaland's mindset ahead of Norway's game against Wales in Cardiff. "Everything is fine," he said. Rúben Dias, stern-faced, shut down a question at a Portugal news conference.

Manchester City women's manager Andree Jeglertz became the first City employee to take questions about the Premier League verdict at a news conference on Wednesday, held to preview their game against Real Madrid. "The thing the club has been presented, is the information we have inside of our group," he said.

"We can't talk about anything else and we don't need to talk about anything else at the moment."

It's likely to be a similar message when Maresca sits down with reporters for the first time next week. He's due to speak for the first time at his next scheduled news conference on Friday, Oct. 9, two days before the trip to play Liverpool at Anfield.

Through the lens of the Premier League's statement, this next fixture has taken on added intensity and spice given Liverpool that have finished second behind City three times in the last 15 years. Of all the clubs who feel most wronged by all this, Liverpool are close to the top of the list.

Amid all the noise, Man City have told their staff to plough on. It may be easier said than done.

stories.headline: Ducks sign Tristan Luneau to $43.2M extension after 14 NHL games
stories.summary: The Ducks have signed defenseman Tristan Luneau to a six-year contract extension worth $43.2 million after just 14 career NHL appearances.
stories.body:
ANAHEIM, Calif. -- The Anaheim Ducks have signed promising young defenseman Tristan Luneau to a six-year contract extension worth $43.2 million after just 14 NHL appearances.

The Ducks announced the deal Thursday with the 22-year-old Luneau, whose promising career has been slowed by injury. Now healthy and ready for a full-time NHL role, he inked a long-term deal with the team that drafted him in the second round in 2022.

Luneau was the Quebec major junior league's top defenseman in the 2022-23 season and he made the Ducks' roster out of training camp the following fall. He came down with a viral infection that winter while practicing with Canada's national junior team, however, forcing him to miss the rest of the year.

Anaheim took a deliberate approach with Luneau's health for the past two seasons, keeping him with its AHL affiliate in San Diego for most of that time. But the Ducks never wavered in their belief that Luneau will be an above-average defenseman, and they proved it with a long-term contract for a player who suited up in just one game for the NHL club last season.

Luneau will be expected to play a significant role this season for the Ducks, who lost four veteran defensemen -- Jacob Trouba, captain Radko Gudas, John Carlson and Olen Zellweger -- from last season's already mediocre blue line group over the summer.

Anaheim general manager Pat Verbeek moved aggressively to lock up Luneau after being burned repeatedly in restricted free agency over the offseason.

Verbeek spent months failing to reach a deal with center Leo Carlsson, who then signed a $90 million offer sheet with Philadelphia that briefly made him the NHL's highest-paid player before Anaheim matched it. Carlsson is among the best young centers in hockey, but his deal is worth much more than he was expected to get as a restricted free agent -- as is the five-year, $36 million deal given to Pavel Mintyukov by Verbeek after other teams began to sniff around the Russian defenseman in the wake of Carlsson's massive offer sheet.

Verbeek then signed high-scoring forward Cutter Gauthier to a six-year, $81 million extension last month, but the resulting salary cap constraints from Verbeek's summer of misadventure effectively forced the Ducks to waive 22-goal scorer Chris Kreider, damaging their depth.

Luneau will join Jackson LaCombe and Mintyukov as the new core of the Ducks' defense. Rising star LaCombe agreed to an eight-year, $72 million extension a year ago.

Anaheim ended a seven-year playoff drought last spring, advancing to the second round under coach Joel Quenneville. The Ducks open the regular season Friday at Vegas before their home opener Sunday against Florida.

stories.headline: Lynx's Napheesa Collier unsure of future as free agency looms
stories.summary: Two-time MVP runner-up Napheesa Collier is unsure of her future as she enters free agency, saying she loves Minnesota but hasn't had time to think about what's next.
stories.body:
MINNEAPOLIS -- Napheesa Collier downplayed talk about her future with the Minnesota Lynx on Thursday, saying she's still dealing with the emotions of being the first 1-seed to lose to an 8-seed in WNBA playoff history.

"Honestly, I haven't even thought about [my future]," Collier said during her exit interview after having been swept in two games by the New York Liberty. "We lost less than 48 hours ago and we didn't expect to be here, so I really haven't had any time to decompress or anything like that.

"I can tell you I love it here. I love the organization. I love my team and everything like that, but I just haven't had the time to give that any thought."

Last summer, Collier, after finishing second behind A'ja Wilson in the 2025 MVP race for the second year in a row, rejected a multiyear deal in lieu of a one-year contract and will now be highly coveted entering free agency.

Collier admitted she wasn't at her best this season -- averaging 16.8 points and 6.9 rebounds -- after returning July 22 from multiple offseason ankle surgeries. In three previous seasons from 2023 to 2025, Collier averaged at least 20 points per game and seven rebounds per game, while finishing fourth, second and second in the MVP race, respectively.

"I mean, obviously, it wasn't the level that I expected for myself. I'm proud of the work that I put into getting to that point," Collier said. "My ultimate goal is to get back on the court and ultimately to help my team win a championship. Obviously, we fell short of that, so that's hard. But still proud of what I was able to accomplish and more than anything proud of the team as well. Obviously, I wasn't 100%, but I gave 100% of what I was able to."

Added Lynx coach Cheryl Reeve: "Everybody could see Napheesa Collier wasn't Napheesa Collier."

But Collier remains an anchor for the team and a free agent with a major decision that could alter the franchise and the entire WNBA. Every team in the WNBA would seemingly make room for the five-time All-Star, if she wanted a change of scenery.

Collier was a bridge for the organization after former superstar Maya Moore abruptly left the league in 2018, ending the reign of a Lynx dynasty that had won four WNBA titles. The sixth overall pick in the 2019 draft, Collier gave Reeve a franchise player to build a new team around. That journey peaked in 2024, when the Lynx reached the WNBA Finals, where they lost to the Liberty.

Locally, Collier's noncommittal words about her future have sounded familiar to sports fans who've watched former WNBA star Katie Smith, baseball All-Star David Ortiz, former NBA All-Stars Kevin Love and Kevin Garnett and even an entire franchise -- the NHL's North Stars -- pick greener pastures before winning championships in those new spots.

Collier might be added to that list in the months ahead, depending on her next move.

"I would just say thank you for everything," Collier said when asked what she would tell fans who wonder if she's played her last game in Minneapolis. "Again, I don't know what to say about that [potentially leaving] part, but through this season and all my eight years here, continuously, the fans are ... a huge reason why Minnesota is just so amazing, why it's so hard for other teams to play in Target Center, why we love playing here.

"The fans, through everything, have stuck beside us through the highs and lows, no matter what the outside noise is."

If Collier leaves, Reeve will have to build a new team around another young star. Although Olivia Miles struggled throughout the playoffs, the WNBA Rookie of the Year said she learned about herself through the loss.

"I think it was an interesting year," Miles said. "We started off with weird expectations and then we got really good and then it was like, 'OK, you guys should win.' And then it felt like if we didn't win, it was the end of the world, almost.

"I was just navigating all those expectations. I also started off as a rookie who no one really thought would do what I did. And now I'm in MVP conversations and now I have to play at that level. And it was just a roller-coaster of expectations and emotions throughout the whole year."

Reeve has navigated this crossroads with star players in the past, but she said she's confident Collier understands the benefits of staying in Minnesota.

"[Collier] knows exactly what exists here. [She] knows the care, the love, all the things that have been poured into her. She's well aware of all of that," Reeve said. "This is a decision that is probably more than basketball. And so wherever she lands, it's going to be because she thinks whatever she chooses or wherever she chooses is the right place for her.

"Sometimes you stay and sometimes you go because maybe there is something -- I don't want to say better -- but maybe better for her. And that's something that I respect. She signed a one-year deal for a reason. It wasn't a multiyear deal. Whatever she decides, we're both going to be OK."

stories.headline: UFC 332 preview and picks: Why haven't there been more women's fights?
stories.summary: Top storylines and coaches' analysis for UFC 332 in Salt Lake City.
stories.body:
For all of the growth and progress of women's MMA over the past 15 years, the 2026 schedule has raised an uncomfortable -- but glaring -- question: What is happening to women's fights? Saturday's UFC 332 event in Salt Lake City will mark the first UFC event this year headlined by women, when Natalia Silva (20-5-1) and Wang Cong (10-1) meet for the vacant flyweight title. This year's lack of high-profile women's fights (and the excitement that should accompany them) has been impossible to miss. Wang, the 34-year-old Chinese challenger, has certainly felt it in the buildup to Saturday.

"Everyone was talking about how bad this main event is," Wang told ESPN, through an interpreter. "Of course I know about it. I think me and my opponent will prove them wrong, and show this is a fight they need to watch."

The sport could definitely use a boost. According to ESPN Research, the UFC has promoted 415 total bouts this year; 56 have featured women. That 13% split is the lowest mark in a decade.

The last women's fight to headline any UFC event was a non-title bout between Mackenzie Dern and Amanda Ribas in January 2025. For the last women's fight to headline a numbered event, one has to go all the way back to a bantamweight title fight between Amanda Nunes and Irene Aldana in June 2023.

Those trends are unlikely to change if some of the more underlying metrics continue to hold. Women's fights are increasingly being pushed to the prelims portion of events. In 2026, 83% of women's fights have appeared on prelims, compared with 72% in 2024, 61% in 2021 and 54% in 2017.

For their part, both Wang and Silva, a 29-year-old challenger out of Brazil, are predicting a memorable matchup Saturday. Wang is a former professional kickboxer with an aggressive style. Silva is known as more of a matador, but in 2024 when she went against Jessica Andrade, the most aggressive opponent of her UFC career, they won fight of the night.

"For sure, it's going to be a well-fought battle," Silva told ESPN through an interpreter. "She comes in aggressive, which gives me the opportunity to be aggressive as well. What I can tell people is that's going to be an incredible fight."

One thing is undeniable, Wang and Silva have a rare opportunity on Saturday to headline a numbered event with a women's title fight.

More storylines to watch
Gautier is getting the step up in competition he asked for
Ateba Gautier is an athletic, 24-year-old wrecking ball from Cameroon with a 5-0 record in the UFC that includes four knockouts. The combined record of his opponents, however, has been 4-14. That doesn't diminish what Gautier has done, but it's still unknown how he will fare against tougher competition.

For his part, Gautier isn't shying away from challenging himself. Immediately following his last win in May, Gautier called for a fight with former middleweight champion Israel Adesanya -- arguably the greatest 185-pound fighter of all time. The UFC didn't give him Adesanya, but he did get Roman Kopylov, a 35-year-old Russian with 12 UFC bouts. A win wouldn't validate Gautier as a title contender, but it would prove he's ready for greater tests.

Wint could be the sleeper breakout candidate of the card
In terms of fighters who can make an individual splash at UFC 332, Wang and Silva in the main event stand out. Payton Talbott taking on a former champion in Deiveson Figueiredo is an obvious one. Undefeated Jacobe Smith is a finishing machine, and the aforementioned Gautier is in the biggest fight of his career.

Quietly, Anthony Wint could steal the show. Wint's prelim fight against Lucas Armand will be his third in less than two months. He's a former collegiate and NFL linebacker, fighting out of a notoriously talented and striking-oriented gym in Kill Cliff FC. He already is very much on UFC CEO Dana White's radar, having earned his contract on "Contender Series" on Aug. 11. If he does something spectacular, expect White to give it attention in his postfight comments (which in turn, draws everyone's attention).

Coaches' questions for women's flyweight championship
'What is Natalia Silva's game plan under pressure?'

Cong's striking is on point. She is aggressive with it, but she makes mistakes with it as well. I feel like Silva is the more well-rounded fighter, and it's up to her to take advantage of that. If this fight does go to the ground, I think Silva will present bigger problems -- and I see that as a path to victory for her. Wang is going to look for the knockout, and because of that, she will overextend in certain positions. I have a gut feeling Silva is going to work some ground work into this one. Silva is so good at controlling the pace of a fight, but with Cong coming at her so aggressively, I think she'll be forced to try different stuff. It's a pick 'em fight. -- John Wood, Syndicate MMA

Who will own the 'second exchange'?
Silva's path to victory is about space, timing and making Wang reset. Silva needs to use her movement and feints to keep Wang from getting comfortable and building combinations. Silva is best at range, not standing in the pocket. Her counters matter in this matchup. She doesn't just survive Wang's pressure, she scores with midrange kicks and southpaw counters after Wang overcommits. For Wang, it's about pressure without chasing. She needs to cut the cage. Containing Silva becomes the real job. This is where her low kick and body work become weapons. Silva's movement is a huge part of her defense. If Wang can consistently attack the legs and body, she can start shrinking the cage without simply chasing. Who controls what happens after the initial exchange? If Wang attacks, Silva counters and exits, that's Silva's fight. If Wang attacks, Silva tries to exit and Wang cuts her off, those are the moments Wang wants. Whoever imposes their will on that second exchange wins. -- Eric Nicksick, Xtreme Couture

stories.headline: UEFA receives Real Madrid dossier on Barcelona-Negreira case
stories.summary: UEFA has received "a substantial amount of documents" from Real Madrid related to its ongoing inquiry into the Negreira case, European football's governing body said on Thursday.
stories.body:
MADRID -- UEFA has received "a substantial amount of documents" from Real Madrid related to its ongoing inquiry into the Negreira case, European football's governing body said on Thursday.

Payments made by Barcelona to companies linked to José María Enriquez Negreira -- the former vice-president of Spain's Technical Committee of Referees -- over two decades have been subject to a UEFA investigation since 2023, while there is also an ongoing Spanish criminal case.

Barcelona have said the payments, which totaled over €7 million ($7.9m), were made for technical refereeing reports.

- Ronaldo's Portugal walkout is nothing new; he has a long history of rows with coaches

- Source: Mbappé to be available for Clásico

- Raphinha back at Barça, injured in Brazil game

"UEFA can confirm that it has received from Real Madrid CF a substantial amount of documents related to the ongoing investigation into FC Barcelona in the matter involving José María Enríquez Negreira," UEFA confirmed in a statement on Thursday.

"The UEFA Ethics and Disciplinary Inspectors have also received these latest documents which they will assess as part of their ongoing review."

Real Madrid said the dossier included "extensive documentation and evidence regarding events of extraordinary seriousness, which directly affect the integrity of the competition and confidence in the refereeing system."

"Real Madrid C.F. considers it essential that, now that UEFA has this documentation, the investigation proceeds with the utmost urgency until its full conclusion, and that the competent bodies take the appropriate decisions in accordance with the severity of the verified facts," the club said.

"Our club will continue to actively collaborate with UEFA and take all actions within its power to clarify events that it deems incompatible with the principles of integrity, transparency, and fair play that should govern European football."

In May, Madrid president Florentino Pérez said that the club was gathering evidence to submit a dossier to UEFA.

Having previously adopted a conciliatory tone with Barcelona -- saying in 2024 that the two clubs "have to help each other" as they worked together on the proposed European Super League -- Pérez has since been extremely critical of his LaLiga rivals.

"They've stolen seven league [titles] from me," Pérez said in May.

In a statement, Barcelona emphasized that Thursday's development did not equate to "any new proceedings."

"The proceedings were initiated in 2023, with the appointment of two investigators who have since carried out the action they deemed appropriate," Barcelona said. "The Club has always complied with all their requests. These proceedings have not been reopened because they have never been closed.

"The UEFA statement confirms receipt of documentation submitted by Real Madrid and indicates that the investigators will assess it within the framework of the existing investigation. The same text expressly refers, on two occasions, to an investigation and a review that are 'ongoing.' It therefore does not announce the opening, reopening, or reactivation of any proceedings, nor does it contain any assessment of the substance or value of the documentation provided.

"It is up to the investigators to determine what action, if any, they consider appropriate regarding this documentation. As of today, they have not made any new requests to FC Barcelona nor have they forwarded Real Madrid's complaint to the Club. Should they do so, the Club will respond accordingly, as it has done up to now.

"In accordance with the applicable legislation governing this matter, these proceedings are subject to the outcome of the criminal case currently being heard in Spain and will continue to be so."

stories.headline: Lando Norris urges F1 and social media giants to help tackle abuse after Franco Colapinto ban feud
stories.summary: Lando Norris called on Formula 1 and social media companies to do more to combat online abuse after the torrent of messages he received following last weekend's Azerbaijan Grand Prix.
stories.body:
Lando Norris called on Formula 1 and social media companies to do more to combat online abuse after the torrent of messages he received following last weekend's Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

The comment sections of Norris' social media channels were filled with thousands of negative and hateful messages after he said in a postrace interview that Alpine driver Franco Colapinto should be banned for causing the collision that took his McLaren out of the race.

Two days after the event in Baku, Norris publicly apologized for his postrace comments in a message shared with his 11.9 million followers on Instagram.

Speaking ahead of this weekend's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, Norris explained why he made the apology and called on the sport, social media channels and drivers to do more to prevent extreme comments, including death threats.

"I said what I wanted to Franco, and he's the only one really that I need to share my opinion with and share my apology with," Norris said. "I don't need to do it on social media, and I don't feel like I need to use social media to do such a thing, but at the same time, there obviously was a lot of that noise and stuff in the background, and I thought it was only sensible to announce or show that I made that apology.

"But yeah, at the same time, I do still see social media at times, and I saw some bits, some not so good, some better, but sadly that's what we deal with. I think a lot of sports deal with [it], some of it's down to just passion, and that's what you always have in sports.

"I think you see a lot more of it because social media is such an easy thing to share your opinions on. And to a certain extent, I completely respect it, but obviously to the extent of online abuse, death threats, all those things, those are things that I think are way too far beyond being a fan of a sport, or a driver, or a person, or an athlete, whatever it is.

"There's a line, but it's not new, it's something that's been around every sport for a long time, and I think just highlights more the fact that social media platforms, sports, need to do more, and maybe the people, the drivers, athletes, whoever, more to stop this kind of stuff from happening, because some people can deal with it much better than others."

Norris said the reaction he received on social media would not stop him from speaking his mind, even though he regretted his postrace comments in Baku.

"I should never have said the sort of stuff that I said, so I get why some people might have been more unhappy, let's just say upset, which is understandable," he added.

"Obviously there's that line which was crossed at times, quite a lot, which is not just being upset at someone, this is much, much worse.

"But I think I'm always happy, in general, in speaking my mind, and saying if I like things, don't like things, if I agree with things or not. I know I'm not able to please everyone, and you're never going to have everyone on your side, so I think that's normal enough, that's life, and that's what you have to come around to accept at the end of the day."

- Lewis Hamilton hits out at Ferrari hierarchy in Fred Vasseur defence: 'Point fingers somewhere else'

- Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia: Where were today's drivers when F1 last raced at Sepang?

- Max Verstappen steps in for GT race at Portimão amid two F1 triple-headers

Colapinto accepted Norris' apology earlier this week, but on Thursday said he was surprised the McLaren driver chose to be so public with his criticism after the race.

"I think he was in the heat of the moment ... He knows what comments create because he suffered from it," Colapinto said.

"He was probably the driver that was speaking the most about hate a couple of years ago, just a few seasons ago. So I was very surprised. But then, of course, he apologised.

"Unfortunately, he also got a lot of hate from it. But I also felt it's a tricky situation with the outside world. And that's why I think we need to be a bit safe inside about the things we say. And I understand it in the heat of the moment to say things like that."

Colapinto's fanbase has proved particularly vocal online and as recently as the Spanish Grand Prix last month turned on his Alpine teammate Pierre Gasly, with abuse that included messages sent to the Frenchman's family and girlfriend.

Asked what his message to those posting the negative comments online would be, Colapinto said: "My message is always the same, that they sometimes don't realise what you can create by writing in your keyword, and that we are humans, and it's not easy for us when we get these kind of things.

"I think it always goes to Argentinians, but we miss that it doesn't come only from Argentinians. It comes a lot from them, I fully agree. It doesn't just come from them, and they are extremely passionate, and they support me a lot. And it's bad, and they are bad many times, but it comes from all the world, and from many other fanbases.

"I don't know if we are not seeing it, I get loads of it and no one ever talks about it. I mean, it's fine because I don't look at social media too much. I don't go into it. But I know it affects a lot of people, and a lot of drivers, and a lot of families more than me.

"I hope that they improve. I've been asking for a long time. It's tricky for us drivers to control it. I think we are the ones to not do them more. But we are also really striving to improve the situation by ourselves. Because we try -- for me, it's been since last year that I've been talking about it. I am doing my best, but it's tricky."

In 2023 F1's governing body, the FIA, set up the United Against Online Abuse (UAOA) commission, which as recently as this year's British Grand Prix received the collective support of all 22 drivers in F1.

On its website, the UAOA says it "aims to design, develop and implement practical actions that can protect the integrity of sports across the world as safe and inclusive spaces for competitors, officials, journalists, and fans alike."

stories.headline: Banned and crowned: Isaac Heeney wins Swans' best and fairest
stories.summary: Isaac Heeney has been named Sydney's best and fairest, but he and fellow Sydney stars were notable absentees from the club's end-of-season awards night.
stories.body:
An absent Isaac Heeney has been crowned Sydney's best and fairest as the spectre of sexual assault allegations continues to loom over the AFL club.

Heeney was not at Sydney Town Hall to accept his third consecutive Bob Skilton medal, having requested to skip the club's Thursday awards night.

Chad Warner, Nick Blakey, James Jordon and Riley Bice were also absent after serving a club-imposed suspension with Heeney throughout the finals.

Despite missing Round 24 and two finals -- which also counted for award calculations -- Heeney polled 431 votes to comfortably claim the club's highest individual annual honour ahead of ruck Brodie Grundy (400) and key forward Charlie Curnow (398).

Four of the suspended Swans finished in the top 10 of the count, with Warner placing fourth ahead of Blakey (seventh) and Jordon (10th).

The club had opted against changing eligibility and voting criteria for the Bob Skilton medal, following suit after the AFL did the same with the Brownlow Medal.

The league did not invite Heeney or Warner to last week's Brownlow ceremony.

In his awards ceremony speech, Swans chairman Andrew Pridham said the reasoning behind the club's eligibility criteria was two-fold - protecting the integrity of votes; and ensuring off-field matters were separate from on-field performance.

"We do not believe it would have been appropriate to retrospectively remove votes that have already been cast owing to the subsequent incident," Pridham said.

"The medals awarded tonight acknowledge on-field performance across the season.

"Erasing a season of football after the fact would, in our opinion, be inappropriate and in excess of a sanction.

"I can assure you that we did not make any decisions we have made in recent times like that.

"I respect that some people in this room and beyond may not agree with where we have landed tonight.

"It has been very, very difficult, but let me be equally clear that these decisions to allow the players to remain eligible does not diminish our concern and respect for everyone involved in this."

Independent of the AFL-endorsed club bans for what the Swans termed a "serious breach of expected club behaviour and standards", a police investigation into an alleged sexual assault at the Pullman Hotel is ongoing.

Detectives in early September travelled to NSW to interview a 30-year-old Maroubra man, a 25-year-old Paddington man and two Randwick men aged 25 and 26.

It is understood the men interviewed were Heeney, Warner, Jordon and Blakey.

No charges have been laid. AAP is not suggesting any wrongdoing on the part of the suspended players.

The five banned players have since returned to Swans headquarters after serving their suspension and individually offered apologies to colleagues and teammates following their team's preliminary final loss to Fremantle.

Heeney was the only player after the club meeting to address media and did so with a brief statement.

"It was really nice to address the whole club," the 30-year-old said on September 23.

"Extremely thankful they could give us their time and understanding, so yeah, it was really good."

Victoria Police's eight-week timeline prediction - which was first flagged on September 2 - on their investigation into the Pullman Hotel incident takes in the free agency and trade period (October 2-14).

All five players are contracted for next year, with Blakey signed to the club until 2031.

Warner and Jordon come off contract at the end of 2027, while Heeney and Bice are signed until the end of 2028.

stories.headline: St. Louis up to 2nd place with unbeaten run now at 17 games
stories.summary: Simon Becher and Tomas Ostrak each scored late in the second half as St. Louis City SC beat the New York Red Bulls 3-0 on Wednesday night.
stories.body:
Simon Becher and Tomas Ostrak each scored late in the second half as St. Louis City SC beat the New York Red Bulls 3-0 on Wednesday night.

St. Louis (13-6-8) extended its unbeaten streak to 17 matches in MLS play and moved up to second place in MLS' Western Conference table.

New York (9-12-6) entered having conceded just two goals in its last four games, with Ethan Horvath recording three shutouts.

The Red Bulls had won their last two games, but were without rising stars Adri Mehmeti and Julian Hall for the game, with the pair away on national team duty for the United States.

Rafael Navarro opened the scoring just five minutes into the game when he redirected Conrad Wallem's header across the goal.

Becher capitalized on a New York turnover deep in its own half to make it 2-0 in the 87th minute. Ostrak sent in a rebound in stoppage time.

Roman Bürki made four saves to earn his third clean sheet of the season for St. Louis.

It was the first time New York and St. Louis have met during the regular season.

St. Louis hosts the LA Galaxy next on Oct. 11, while the Red Bulls play San Diego FC at home the day before.

Information from The Associated Press was used in this report.

stories.headline: Ivan: Nathan Cleary can get even better after Dally M
stories.summary: Ivan Cleary has spoken of the horror of watching his son Nathan's leg injury, and a belief he can still get better again after winning his first Dally M.
stories.body:
Ivan Cleary has admitted watching his son Nathan suffer a badly broken leg marked one of the hardest days of his career, feeling the line between father and coach blurred for the first time.

But the veteran Penrith mentor is insistent his son Nathan still has more levels to attain once he returns from his injury, following his landmark Dally M victory on Wednesday night.

Cleary's Dally M triumph completed the Penrith halfback's rugby league box set, having now claimed every major team and individual honour available to him by age 28.

Unable to attend in person after being released from hospital following emergency surgery on his leg, the Panthers halfback collected the game's top honour while in a wheelchair at home.

Coach Ivan also appeared emotional during Nathan's pre-recorded speech, after the trophy was hand-delivered to the halfback earlier in the day.

"His voice perked up from what it's been the past couple of days," Ivan told AAP.

"It's a pretty amazing award. You don't play the game for individual awards, but it's certainly nice to be recognised.

"Particularly this award, it's pretty much the No.1 award in the game."

Reminded that his son had now scaled virtually every possible mountain in the sport, the Penrith coach insisted there were still improvements left in his son's game.

"It's crazy," Ivan said.

"I know he'd say it and I probably think a bit the same. You don't reflect too much when it's still going on. But when you put it like that, it's amazing.

"But I know there is so much more to come as well, and I know he thinks that way as well."

Nathan has received positive early news from surgeons after the operation on his compound fracture and dislocated ankle, as a result of a hip-drop tackle in Sunday's preliminary-final loss to Newcastle.

He will soon undergo surgery on other foot after fighting through a broken bone to play the Knights, but Penrith are hopeful he will be right for round one in 2027.

"Sunday was definitely one of the harder days I have been through," coach Cleary said.

"It's the first time where the line of dad and coach got a bit blurred. And the loss, I guess we have had a lot of good days so you can't have it all your way.

"Very emotional, but life goes on."

Footage has also emerged of fullback Dylan Edwards not only being horrified by the graphic injury at first, but then also trying to stop Nathan from seeing it.

"I was just trying to keep him calm as I could," Edwards said.

"To his credit he is a tough person. And the way he was handling that was incredible.

"It was gut-wrenching, something you're not used to seeing on the footy field."

Edwards, meanwhile, is still hopeful of being able to represent Australia at the World Cup after avoiding knee surgery following a PCL injury in the loss.

"I'm not sure, I have to talk to Kevvie (coach Kevin Walters)," Edwards said, while wearing a brace at the Dally Ms.

stories.headline: Joey Porter happy for fresh start with Cowboys, eyes Sunday debut
stories.summary: Joey Porter Jr. says he hopes to make his debut for the Cowboys on Sunday, when they play the Texans.
stories.body:
FRISCO, Texas -- When the week began, Joey Porter Jr. thought he would be playing Thursday night for the Pittsburgh Steelers against the Cleveland Browns. Now, he hopes to make his Dallas Cowboys debut Sunday against the Houston Texans.

"We're just trying to take things day by day," Porter said after his first practice in Dallas, "and if everything looks good, then we should be out there."

Porter was at the movie theater watching Brad Pitt's "Heart of the Beast" when he got word of the trade. The Cowboys gave up a 2027 sixth-round pick and a 2028 second-rounder to acquire Porter, marking the third deal the organizations have made since May 2025 (George Pickens, Broderick Jones).

Early Thursday morning, he was on a plane to join his new team, ending his run with the Steelers, who drafted him in the second round of the 2023 draft.

Porter was hoping for an extension with the Steelers, and the saga lasted throughout the offseason and into training camp while he dealt with a back injury. Porter said it was more his call not to play in against the Browns, but added that his back was "feeling better."

Porter is not listed on the Cowboys' injury report.

"It was a hard process; a lot of ups and downs," Porter said. "Definitely felt disrespected, definitely felt undervalued. But that's the old news now. That's how I look at it. I'm on to new beginnings, new chapters. And like I said, I'm a Cowboy. I'm in Dallas, so I'm happy about that."

Porter will have to wait for a possible extension from the Cowboys, too. Still, he said he would be open to finishing his career in Dallas.

"I'm down with it if they are. I want to finish my career here," Porter said. "So hopefully, I just perform like how I know how to perform and do what I do, and I'm going to let everything take care of the rest."

Through three games, the Cowboys are 25th in points allowed (27.3) and 30th in yards (387). The Cowboys are one of four teams without an interception.

With Cobie Durant (hamstring) expected to miss his second game and Shavon Revel Jr. not practicing much this week because of knee and ankle issues, the Cowboys almost need to have Porter immediately.

"This is more about you get a chance to get a young corner that's got elite cover skills that can come in and add to a group that's depleted right now with injuries is always good," coach Brian Schottenheimer said. "But I think change of scenery is good."

It worked for Pickens, who had career highs in catches (93), yards (1,429) and touchdowns (nine) last season with the Cowboys.

Defensive coordinator Christian Parker used the term "boundary eraser" in his evaluation of Porter when he came out of Penn State. Though Porter has a reputation for his man-to-man skills, Parker said he saw him do enough work with the Steelers to know it won't be a difficult adjustment to the scheme. Parker said even if the Cowboys are in zone, they have some man principles.

"When you have guys who can erase one-on-one matchups on the backside, then you can do different things to manipulate coverage," Parker said. "You can add plus ones in different areas of the field. You can add plus ones in run defense. You don't want to put guys on the island the whole game, but you can definitely kind of move some pieces around and make other things better."

Porter has just three career interceptions, but since 2023, he is ranked 13th among defensive backs when targeted as the nearest defender, allowing just a 56% completion rate, according to Next Gen Stats. He has also committed the most penalties by a defender in that span (36, including 14 pass interference flags).

"The most important thing is not letting the guy that's getting targeted catch the football. The next step is catching it yourself," Parker said. "So, we're going to get him in the building and onboard him and see where he's at with those things. We won't be the first coaches that have tried to improve those things with him, but he does a lot of things at a high level that'll give us a chance to improve that."

Porter said creating turnovers is his next step.

"I think I've shown that I could take wide receivers out the game," he said. "Now, I just want my ball production to be up, and I'm going to strive for that."

The Cowboys also hope the addition of Porter helps their pass rush, which has accounted for just two sacks in three games, by forcing quarterbacks to hold the ball longer.

"I think rushing [and] coverage are always married together," Parker said. "There's coverage sacks; there's also quick wins. So, they all benefit each other. If you have a premium rusher, of course that helps the coverage. If you have a premium coverage, that helps the rush."
